input.situation_text: Two invoices for same job: one matches approved £210 from contractor of record; second from different payee H&S Domestic Services for £324 incl extra labour, same job ref. Landlord pays directly.

lessons.situation: A contractor who completed an approved cleaning job emails to say their invoice has been sent to the agency's operator, while the request is on hold waiting for the provider and the system is prompting the operator to check whether a reply is needed or to return the request to auto mode.
lessons.action: When the contractor confirms the invoice has been sent, no reply to them is needed. Move the task to the result/completed state, mark the request as completed for final checks, and forward the invoice to the landlord with a short covering note. Record that landlord confirmation is needed, then close the request once the final checks are done.
lessons.rationale: A contractor's invoice notification is an informational closing message rather than a question, so the right response is to progress closeout and pass the invoice to the landlord instead of replying or leaving the request on hold.

lessons.situation: A contractor attended a scheduled repair visit, but the system showed no work results afterwards and flagged the job for checking; the contractor's invoice note then described the fault found, the fix and a successful test.
lessons.action: When no work results have been logged after a completed visit, check the contractor's invoice note for the findings and outcome, and treat it as the completion record if it confirms the fault, the fix and a passing test. Move the task to Result, mark the request completed and start the final checks. Skip optional document uploads that aren't needed, recording the reason. Then request the landlord's confirmation before closing.
lessons.rationale: The invoice note can serve as proof of completion when no separate report exists, and the landlord should still confirm before the job is closed.

lessons.situation: A maintenance request was paused while awaiting landlord approval to send the agency's usual appliance contractor, and the landlord has since replied with a clear, unconditional approval.
lessons.action: Read the landlord's reply and, if it is an unambiguous approval, record it as approved and return the request to auto mode with no further reply to the landlord. Then move to provider selection, assign the proposed contractor, email the tenant to say the contractor will contact them to arrange a visit, and send the contractor the job details and tenant contact information.
lessons.rationale: A clear approval needs no further response to the landlord, so the job should resume automatically and go straight to contractor assignment and notifications to avoid delays.

lessons.situation: A contractor who missed a confirmed appointment and was rebooked has emailed to report the plumbing job completed (part replaced, tenants confirming the other fault is fine), while the request was on hold awaiting the provider and flagged to check whether a response is needed before returning to auto mode.
lessons.action: When a contractor reports completion after a rescheduled or missed visit, confirm the report covers all reported faults and that the tenant has not raised any outstanding issue. If no reply to the contractor is needed, record that the landlord pays the contractor directly, close the task as completed without agency payment, and return the request to auto mode.
lessons.rationale: A completion report that addresses every fault needs no further chasing, and noting the landlord's direct payment arrangement keeps the agency from processing an invoice it will not pay.

lessons.situation: A checkout-clean estimate was requested from a contractor and the job was placed on hold waiting for the provider; the contractor then replied by email with the estimate and asked to be told if the attachment had not come through.
lessons.action: When a contractor replies after a hold for provider response, open the email and confirm the estimate attachment is present and matches the requested scope (clean, removal of dumped items, carpet clean). If it is, reply to the contractor confirming receipt and telling them to proceed, record the estimate as approved, and keep the job on hold with a 'hold for works' note until the works are completed instead of returning it to auto mode.
lessons.rationale: Answering the contractor promptly with clear confirmation avoids delay, and holding the job for works stops automation from chasing or progressing it before the clean is done.

input.subject: Invoices TS-0881 / TS-0882 – job HC-14-310, 19 Coppice Road, Ludlow Heath ZZ5 7ZZ
input.body:
Hello,

Thank you for your email of 6 October regarding job HC-14-310 (immersion thermostat/element replacement at 19 Coppice Road, Ludlow Heath, ZZ5 7ZZ).

We received two invoices for this job:
- TS-0881, payee Thermo-Serve Ltd, £210.00 incl. VAT – this matches the approved quote.
- TS-0882, payee H&S Domestic Services, £324.00 incl. VAT, including 2 hours' extra labour.

The landlord approved Thermo-Serve Ltd at £210 only. Please could you confirm which invoice is the valid one, who H&S Domestic Services are, and why TS-0882 was issued? Additional labour was not part of the approval, so it cannot be put forward without justification and the landlord's separate agreement.

A member of our team may also call you on the number we hold on file to confirm. Neither invoice will be passed for payment until this is clarified.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance team

Dear Ms Ferrer,

Regarding the immersion thermostat/element replacement at 19 Coppice Road (job HC-14-310), which you approved for Thermo-Serve Ltd at £210.

On 6 October we received two invoices for this job from the Thermo-Serve email address:
- TS-0881, payee Thermo-Serve Ltd, £210.00 incl. VAT – matches your approval.
- TS-0882, payee H&S Domestic Services, £324.00 incl. VAT – a different payee from the contractor on the job, £114 above the approved amount, and includes 2 hours' extra labour that was not quoted.

Please do not pay either invoice for now. We are confirming with Thermo-Serve, using the contact details we already hold, which invoice is valid. We will come back to you with a checked invoice, or with any request for extra cost for your decision, and expect to update you within 3 working days. If you receive any request directly to pay a different account, please let us know before acting on it.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance team
